headline: Foundation-model encoders and benchmarks rank enzymes, reactions and mutants for experimental follow-up
label: Learned Enzyme Candidate Prioritization
summary: New enzyme-focused models and a mutant-prioritization benchmark with a 150-mutant validation test how well learned scores rank candidates for experiments.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned scoring of enzyme-related candidates: reaction-enzyme pairs (RIVER), kinetic parameters (KineCouple, AlphaEnzyme), thermostability and growth temperature (StableProt), and mutants (EnzyArena). Several works build on frozen pretrained encoders, including ProtT5/MolT5 in KineCouple, SaProt with Foldseek 3Di tokens in StableProt, and a structure-grounded foundation model in AlphaEnzyme. Evaluation is the newer emphasis: EnzyArena groups kinetic data by campaign, compares 20 models for mutant prioritization, finds zero-shot consensus best, and adds a 150-mutant experimental check, while the generative-reaction study uses a reaction-disjoint benchmark. HEIWA, which injects solvent information into ESM3 embeddings, fits only loosely, as a representation refinement rather than a ranking method.
